what: Depth-curriculum ladder of run dyn_latq_v15, 18 800 steps. (a) the gate-probe depth t_max as a step function (dotted verticals = gate unlocks, red = gate stalls) with the sampled training-episode depth as a light backdrop; (b) probe e_fin and the 21-step mean of the training e_fin, log scale; (c) the sampled training depth T over time.
one_line_reading: The gate unlocks depth monotonically 1 -> 16 over 15 events ending at step 17 500, and the probe error falls to 0.167 while the training step reaches e_fin = 0.096; the sampler never stops drawing shallow episodes, so this curve measures the gate trajectory, not the training mixture.

source.origin_note: the only surviving copy of this run log is the workstation copy shipped in this package (data/raw/latent/)

method: line-type regexes over the raw log; [gate-probe] gives the ladder, [dyn_latq] gives training episodes, [gate-dep]/[gate-tf] give gate transitions. The two depth quantities are separate marks.
caveats: dyn_latq_v15.log is NOT on the server; docs/DEVIATIONS.md:425 states it was kept, but the file no longer exists there. Only the workstation copy survives (this figure's source).
'T=16' appears only in the gate-probe line; the deepest *training* episode in the log is T=15 (3 rows). The run was stopped at step 18 800 before its 32 000-step schedule finished.

the ladder's own reading is e_fin at the gate (0.167 at step 18 750); the training-step reading e_fin = 0.096 belongs to a T=3 episode and is not the depth-16 result. Do not quote 0.096 as the depth-16 error.
deviates from the brief's 'twin axis' suggestion: e_fin got its own panel because a shared frame made the ladder and the error curves unreadable.
